hook.text: A raw egg is liquid. A boiled egg is solid. Nothing was added—the proteins just changed shape.

buildup.text: Denaturation unfolds a protein's 3D structure. Heat, acid, salt, and mechanical force can all trigger it.

discovery.text: Whipping egg whites traps air in unfolded proteins. That's how meringue gets its structure—mechanical denaturation.

twist.text: Denaturation is usually irreversible. You can't unboil an egg—the proteins have tangled permanently.

climax.text: Overcooking meat squeezes water out of denatured proteins. That's why a well-done steak is dry.

punchline.text: Cooking is controlled denaturation. Go too far and you ruin the food.

quiz.question: Why does overcooked meat become dry?
